conclusion: Based on available evidence, Nora Vale is the most likely responsible party for removing the laboratory prototype. Visual evidence (V04) shows a teal-coated person with the prototype at East Exit at 18:14. Badge records (D01) show Nora Vale's credential was used to enter East Corridor at 18:10 and exit East Exit at 18:14, consistent with the visual timeline. Nora Vale is assigned a teal work coat per shift assignments (D03). Her witness statement claiming she only visited the corridor without taking anything is contradicted by V04 showing prototype possession.
limitations: Badge credentials do not constitute biometric identification (D03) - another person could have used Nora Vale's badge
Coat colors are assigned per shift, not unique identifiers (D03) - another person could have worn a teal coat
Theft moment was not captured on any camera - exact removal time and method unknown
Service Corridor is an unmonitored blind spot (V10, D03) - cannot confirm whether this route was used
Single timestamp snapshots do not provide continuous alibis for other staff members

alternative_explanations.explanation: Badge impersonation - another person used Nora Vale's badge while wearing a teal coat
alternative_explanations.reasoning: Requires coordinated deception; no evidence of badge theft or sharing

alternative_explanations.explanation: Authorized removal - prototype legitimately removed with authorization not in available evidence
alternative_explanations.reasoning: No supporting documentation found for authorized removal

alternative_explanations.explanation: Coat substitution - another person wore a teal coat assigned to someone else
alternative_explanations.reasoning: Possible given D03 shift assignment note, but less likely than direct involvement
